subtitle: When a Smoke Bomb Shook an Empire

panels.action: Bhagat Singh stands in the gallery of the Central Legislative Assembly, arm mid-swing with a small cylindrical bomb, smoke already curling, legislators frozen in shock around him.

dialogue.text: Delhi, 1929: Bhagat Singh hurls a smoke bomb in the Assembly, not to kill but to be heard, and turns a colonial courtroom into a pulpit of revolt.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली, 1929: भगत सिंह ने असेम्बली में धुआँ बम फेंका – मारने नहीं, अपनी आवाज़ सुनाने, और अदालत को बगावत का मंच बना दिया।

panels.action: Close-up of Bhagat Singh’s calm, determined face in profile, moustache neat, cap shadowing sharp eyes, as he watches a blurred image of the Central Legislative Assembly in the distance.

dialogue.text: By 1929, India seethed. Laws tightened, protests met lathi and prison, and in the shadows a young revolutionary asked: how do you make a deaf empire listen?

i18n.hi: 1929 तक भारत खौल रहा था। कानून कड़े, आंदोलनों पर लाठी–जेल, और अंधेरे में एक नौजवान ने पूछा: बहरे साम्राज्य को सुनाएँ तो कैसे?

panels.shot: wide shot with overlaid ghostly montage feel
panels.action: Bhagat Singh sits at a wooden table under a dim lamp, leaflets, newspapers and a revolver laid out, while ghostly overlays suggest CID agents in trench coats and cameras watching from doorways.

dialogue.text: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association plotted with ink and gunpowder. Police files and hidden cameras trailed them, yet they in turn studied the press, theatre and crowds as their own weapons.

i18n.hi: हिंदुस्तान सोशलिस्ट रिपब्लिकन असोसिएशन स्याही और बारूद से साजिश रच रही थी। पुलिस की फ़ाइलें, गुप्त कैमरे उनके पीछे, पर वे भी प्रेस, रंगमंच और भीड़ों को अपना हथियार बना रहे थे।

panels.action: Over Bhagat Singh’s shoulder we see his hand writing on a leaflet, the words 'it takes a loud voice to make the deaf hear' clearly visible, while a small, carefully crafted bomb shell lies open nearby.

dialogue.text: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt prepared bombs meant to startle, not slaughter. Their own statement stressed design and timing meant only to shake the air and the conscience, not to spill blood.

i18n.hi: भगत सिंह और बटुकेश्वर दत्त ने ऐसे बम बनाए जो दहशत फैलाएँ, कत्लेआम नहीं। बयान में साफ लिखा: यह धमाका हवा और ज़मीर झकझोरने को है, खून बहाने को नहीं।

panels.shot: high wide shot of interior hall
panels.action: A sweeping view of the Central Legislative Assembly in session, colonial officials in white suits and turbans seated at benches as Bhagat Singh stands in the visitors’ gallery, hand slipping into his coat.

dialogue.text: On 8 April 1929, as the Assembly debated further powers for the Raj, two quiet figures took their places in the gallery. Their real audience lay beyond these walls, in the streets and printing presses.

i18n.hi: 8 अप्रैल 1929, राज को और अधिकार देने पर बहस चल रही थी। गैलरी में दो शांत शख़्स बैठे। उनका असली निशाना इन दीवारों से बाहर, सड़कों और छापेखानों में था।

panels.action: Bhagat Singh and an unseen companion each throw a small bomb toward the empty central space of the Assembly; the devices are mid-air as thick smoke erupts and legislators recoil, some ducking under desks.

dialogue.text: The bombs arced gently, falling in clear spaces. Two sharp explosions, then smoke and confusion. No one was killed. The point was shock, the line from their leaflet already choosing its echo.

i18n.hi: बम धीरे से झूल कर खाली जगहों में गिरे। दो तेज धमाके, फिर धुआँ और अफरातफरी। किसी की जान नहीं गई। मक़सद था झटका, पर्चे की पंक्ति पहले ही अपनी गूँज चुन चुकी थी।

panels.action: Bhagat Singh stands straight in the swirling smoke, arm raised, mouth open in a shout, as stunned members and guards turn toward him in a haze of dust and ash.

dialogue.speaker: bhagat_singh
dialogue.text: Inquilab Zindabad!

i18n.hi: इंक़लाब ज़िंदाबाद!

dialogue.text: He shouted for revolution, threw leaflets into the choking air, and then—unlike the assassins the Raj expected—he did not run.

i18n.hi: उसने क्रांति के नारे लगाए, पर्चे उछाले, गला घोंटते धुएँ में… और फिर – राज की उम्मीद के कातिलों से उलट – भागा नहीं।

panels.action: Bhagat Singh calmly extends his wrists toward approaching policemen, face serene, as crumpled leaflets lie scattered on the Assembly floor around his feet.

dialogue.text: Bhagat Singh and Dutt surrendered at once. Their aim lay not in escape but in a platform: a public trial, reported in every paper, where they could explain why they had shaken the House.

i18n.hi: भगत सिंह और दत्त ने तुरंत आत्मसमर्पण किया। उनका निशाना भागना नहीं, मंच था – खुली सुनवाई, हर अख़बार में खबर, जहाँ वे बता सकें क्यों उन्होंने सदन हिलाया।

panels.action: Inside the Sessions Court at Delhi, Bhagat Singh stands in the dock, flanked by policemen, as British officials and Indian lawyers sit facing him, the packed gallery watching intently.

dialogue.text: On 6 June 1929, in the Sessions Court, the accused became the accuser. Their joint statement, carefully drafted, turned the bomb from crime to argument, and the courtroom into a stage.

i18n.hi: 6 जून 1929, सेशंस कोर्ट में मुलज़िम ही मुंसिफ बन बैठे। उनकी तैयार संयुक्त बयानबाज़ी ने बम को जुर्म से तर्क बना दिया, और अदालत को रंगमंच।

panels.action: Close on Bhagat Singh in the dock, speaking firmly, one hand slightly raised, his eyes meeting the unseen gaze of the judge and audience beyond.

dialogue.speaker: bhagat_singh
dialogue.text: It takes a loud voice to make the deaf hear.

i18n.hi: बहरों को सुनाने को ज़ोर की आवाज़ चाहिए।

panels.shot: wide shot with newspapers in foreground
panels.action: Bundles of newspapers roll off a printing press in the foreground, headlines and grainy photographs of Bhagat Singh faintly visible, while in the background he is led in handcuffs through a corridor lined with reporters.

dialogue.text: CID files and British reports later showed what the revolutionaries had counted on: journalists, photographers and political networks carried their words far beyond the walls that confined them.

i18n.hi: सीआईडी फ़ाइलों और अंग्रेज़ी रिपोर्टों ने बाद में वही दिखाया जिस पर क्रांतिकारी टिके थे – पत्रकार, फ़ोटोग्राफ़र, राजनीतिक जाल, उनकी बातों को जेल की दीवारों से बहुत दूर ले गए।

panels.action: In a bare prison cell in Lahore, Bhagat Singh sits cross-legged on a rough blanket, thin mattress rolled aside, writing on sheets of paper as a tin plate of simple food sits untouched.

dialogue.text: Transferring them between Delhi and Punjab, the Raj sought to isolate. Instead, prison became another arena. Singh wrote, debated, and underlined that theirs was a political battle, not a hidden conspiracy.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली–पंजाब के बीच इधर–उधर कर के राज ने उन्हें काटने की सोची। पर जेल ही नया मैदान बन गई। सिंह ने लिखा, बहस की, और साफ किया: यह राजनीतिक लड़ाई है, छुपा षड्यंत्र नहीं।

panels.action: A row of Indian political prisoners, including Bhagat Singh, stand defiantly in a jail ward, refusing food as European prisoners in a separate, better-furnished section look on from a distance.

dialogue.text: Then another decision: a hunger strike. They protested unequal treatment of Indian and European prisoners, demanding political status. What began behind brick and iron soon gripped the country outside.

i18n.hi: फिर एक और फ़ैसला – भूख हड़ताल। वे भारतीय और यूरोपीय कैदियों के unequal सलूक के खिलाफ खड़े हुए, राजनीतिक कैदी का दर्जा माँगा। ईंट–लोहे के पीछे शुरू हुई आग जल्द ही देश भर में फैल गई।

panels.action: Bhagat Singh, visibly thinner, leans on the bars of his cell, supporting a gaunt Jatindra Nath Das who lies weak on a simple cot, a worried Indian warder and another prisoner watching from the shadows.

dialogue.text: The strike stretched into weeks. Some relented; others held on. On 13 September 1929, Jatindra Nath Das died after sixty-three days, his frail body carried from the jail as crowds gathered outside.

i18n.hi: हड़ताल हफ़्तों तक खिंची। कुछ टूटे, कुछ डटे रहे। 13 सितंबर 1929 को जतिंद्र नाथ दास तिरेसठ दिन बाद शहीद हो गए, उनका नाज़ुक जिस्म जेल से उठकर भीड़ के बीच पहुँचा।

panels.action: A massive funeral procession moves through a city street with Das’s coffin draped in cloth, portraits of Bhagat Singh and other revolutionaries held high among a sea of people and banners.

dialogue.text: His funeral drew thousands. Reports, editorials and speeches turned prison food, fetters and discipline into public questions. The hunger strike had made the treatment of political prisoners a national issue.

i18n.hi: उनके अंतिम जुलूस में हज़ारों उमड़े। रिपोर्ट, लेख, भाषण – जेल की रोटी, बेड़ियाँ, सज़ाएँ – सब सार्वजनिक सवाल बन गए। भूख हड़ताल ने राजनीतिक कैदियों का हक़ राष्ट्रीय मुद्दा कर दिया।

panels.action: Inside the Lahore Conspiracy Case tribunal, a panel of British judges sit elevated, papers piled before them, while Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev stand together in the dock under heavy guard.

dialogue.text: Meanwhile, the Lahore Conspiracy Case unfolded. Separate from the Assembly bomb, this tribunal tied Bhagat Singh to earlier actions and to Rajguru and Sukhdev, combing through evidence over long months.

i18n.hi: उधर लाहौर कांस्पिरेसी केस चला। असेम्बली बम से अलग, इस मुकदमे ने भगत सिंह को पुराने घटनाक्रम, राजगुरु और सुखदेव से जोड़ा, महीनों सबूत टटोले गए।

panels.shot: medium shot on Bhagat Singh’s reaction
panels.action: Bhagat Singh listens as a judge reads from a document, his posture upright, expression composed; Rajguru and Sukhdev stand close, faces tense, as policemen watch.

dialogue.text: On 7 October 1930, the tribunal pronounced its verdict. The Complete Proceedings record the sentence: death for Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev, in the name of imperial law and order.

i18n.hi: 7 अक्टूबर 1930 को ट्रिब्यूनल ने फ़ैसला सुनाया। ‘कम्प्लीट प्रोसिडिंग्स’ में दर्ज है – भगत सिंह, राजगुरु, सुखदेव को फाँसी, साम्राज्य के कानून और ‘क़ानून–व्यवस्था’ के नाम पर।

panels.action: In a dim Lahore jail cell, Bhagat Singh sits on his cot, reading a book by lamplight, a faint smile on his face, a noose’s shadow falling long across the wall behind him.

dialogue.speaker: bhagat_singh
dialogue.text: They can kill individuals, but not the ideas they serve.

i18n.hi: वे इंसानों को मार सकते हैं, उन विचारों को नहीं जिनकी वे सेवा करते हैं।

panels.action: A long, narrow corridor of Lahore Central Jail at night, three indistinct figures being led away by warders toward a heavy wooden door, while outside the prison walls a small crowd keeps vigil in the darkness.

dialogue.text: On 23 March 1931, Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged in Lahore. Their bodies were taken away in haste, but the trial records, the leaflets and the echo of that smoke-filled hall remained.

i18n.hi: 23 मार्च 1931 को भगत सिंह, राजगुरु, सुखदेव को लाहौर में फाँसी दी गई। लाशें जल्दबाज़ी में ले जाई गईं, पर मुकदमे की कार्यवाही, पर्चे और धुएँ से भरे उस सदन की गूँज रह गई।

panels.action: A symbolic scene where Bhagat Singh’s figure, semi-transparent, stands above a crowd of later protestors holding placards and newspapers, the outlines of the Assembly and a prison wall faint in the background.

dialogue.text: He chose to speak through a bomb that harmed none, a courtroom that chained him, and a hunger strike that cost a comrade’s life—so that a clear idea might ring louder than the sentence that ended his days.

i18n.hi: उसने ऐसा बम चुना जिसने किसी को चोट न पहुँचाई, ऐसी अदालत जो उसे ज़ंजीरों में बाँधती थी, और ऐसी भूख हड़ताल जो साथी की जान ले गई – ताकि एक साफ़ विचार, उसकी मौत की सज़ा से भी ऊँची आवाज़ में गूँज सके।

subtitle_i18n.en: When a Smoke Bomb Shook an Empire
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब एक धुएँ के बम ने साम्राज्य हिला दिया
